1.title: The People Element: Ecosystems, Change, Stakeholders and Culture
1.text: Welcome to Module three: The People Element: Ecosystems, Change, Stakeholders and Culture. It covers the exam area The people element. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Define organizational ecosystem, project ecosystem, change management, stakeholder, culture, collaboration and co-creation, leadership and management. Explain the difference between people within the project and people affected by the project. Explain change management and why it matters. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The people element (fourteen percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: Why a people element
1.text: Why a people element. prince two seven added people as a full element because projects succeed or fail through people. The method must be applied by, and for, real people with different views, cultures and interests.

1.title: Ecosystems
1.text: Ecosystems. Organizational ecosystem. The wider organization(s) around the project: structure, culture, other projects and programmes, and the people and groups it affects. Project ecosystem. The people and groups connected to the project itself: the project management team and the stakeholders around it.

1.title: Ecosystems, continued
1.text: Ecosystems. The figure shows this: The organizational ecosystem around the project ecosystem.

1.title: People within the project and people affected by it
1.text: People within the project and people affected by it. People within the project. The project management team: board members, project manager, team managers, project assurance and support. People affected by the project. Users, operations staff, customers, other teams: those who change how they work or use the result. Exam tip: Within equals the project management team. Affected equals everyone who feels the change. A stakeholder can be either.

1.title: Change, stakeholders and culture
1.text: Change, stakeholders and culture. Change management. Helping people move from the current way of working to the new one, and keeping the benefits. Stakeholder. Anyone who can affect, is affected by, or believes they are affected by the project. Culture. The shared values, attitudes and behaviors of a group. Why change management matters: a project can deliver the product on time and still fail if people do not adopt it. The change management approach (part of the P I D) says how the project will support people through the change.

1.title: Stakeholder engagement
1.text: Stakeholder engagement. Identify stakeholders, analyze their interest and influence, plan how to engage them, engage and review. Engagement is continuous, not a one-off. The communication management approach (Module four) records the plan.

1.title: Collaboration, co-creation, leadership and management
1.text: Collaboration, co-creation, leadership and management. Collaboration. People working together toward shared objectives. Co-creation. Involving users and stakeholders in building the solution with the team. Leadership. Inspiring and guiding people toward a vision; influence. Management. Planning, organizing, controlling and delivering within agreed limits. Exam tip: Leadership equals direction and inspiration (people). Management equals planning and control (work). A good project manager needs both. Exam tip: Stakeholder is the widest word: it covers people within the project and people affected by it, and even those who only believe they are affected.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Warehouse staff will have to change how they scan items after the project delivers a new system. What are they in relation to the project? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: People affected by the project. They are affected by the project.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) A stakeholder can affect the project. (two) A stakeholder can be affected by the project. (three) Only the project board members are stakeholders. (four) Stakeholders are only people inside the project team. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one and two. A stakeholder can affect, or be affected by, the project.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. blank describes the shared values, attitudes and behaviors of a group. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Culture. That is culture.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A project delivered a new tool on time, but staff keep using the old one. Which people concept was neglected? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Change management. Helping people adopt the change is change management.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which pair correctly matches leadership and management? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Leadership is inspiring and guiding people; management is planning and controlling the work. Leadership inspires; management plans and controls.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Where is the plan for supporting people through the change recorded? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: In the change management approach, part of the P I D. The change management approach is part of the P I D.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Define a stakeholder. Answer: Anyone who can affect, is affected by, or believes they are affected by the project. Question two. What is the project ecosystem? Answer: The people and groups connected to the project itself. Question three. What is change management? Answer: Helping people move from the current way of working to the new one and keeping the benefits.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Define culture. Answer: The shared values, attitudes and behaviors of a group. Question five. What is co-creation? Answer: Involving users and stakeholders in building the solution with the team. Question six. Which management product records how the project will support change? Answer: The change management approach (in the P I D).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Ecosystems: organizational (wider organization) and project (people connected to the project). Within or affected: project management team or everyone who feels the change. Stakeholder: can affect, be affected, or believe they are affected. Change management: move people to the new way; P I D approach. Leadership or management: inspire people or plan and control work.
